title: Brazilian President Lula invites Marcos to visit Brazil
summary: Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva invited President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. to visit Brazil next year, as the two countries recently held bilateral talks in Manila.

blocks.text: Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva invited President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. to visit Brazil next year, as the two countries recently held bilateral talks in Manila.
Da Silva made the statement during a press briefing on Sunday as he concludes his two-day visit to the Philippines, according to GMA News Bea Pinlac's social media post.
He said Marcos was among the heads of state he invited to visit Brazil.
“We’re inviting everyone to come and visit Brazil,” Da Silva said, which was translated in English by a device provided by the Brazil delegation.
He added that Brazil aims to promote and collaborate with other countries in “exploration, transformation, industrialization,” among others.
Da Silva also hopes that Brazil will be a "definitive partner of ASEAN."
Malacañang said it has yet to confirm Brazil's invitation through the Department of Foreign Affairs.
Da Silva's visit coincided with the 49th ASEAN Summit and Related Summits being held from November 15 to 17 in Pasay City.
Brazil, meanwhile, is a sectoral dialogue partner of ASEAN.
The bilateral meeting between the Philippines and Brazil tackled ways to enhance relations between the two countries.
The talks of the two leaders covered cooperation in multilateral forums and among countries of the Global South, according to the Presidential Communications Office.
Lula’s state visit also marks the first time a sitting Brazilian president visited the Philippines.
It also coincides with the 80th anniversary of diplomatic relations between the two countries this year.—Mariel Celine Serquiña/RF, GMA News
